questions.question: Which platform has the Securities and Exchange Board of India partnered with to reduce unclaimed assets in the Indian securities market?

questions.question: Where does the rupee go the most and where does the rupee mostly come from, as per the Budget 2025-26?

options.text: Rupee goes the most to Defence, and comes mostly from Income Tax.
Rupee goes the most to Major Subsidies, and comes mostly from GST & Other Taxes.
Rupee goes the most to Interest Payments, and comes mostly from Corporation Tax.
Rupee goes the most to States’ Share of Taxes and Duties, and comes mostly from Borrowing and Other Liabilities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rupee goes the most to States’ Share of Taxes and Duties, and comes mostly from Borrowing and Other Liabilities.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **As per the Budget 2025-26, the highest government expenditure is on States’ Share of Taxes and Duties__ (22%), while the largest revenue source is __Borrowing and Other Liabilities__ (24%).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The largest expenditure component is the States’ Share of Taxes and Duties__, which accounts for 22% of the total rupee expenditure.
 
• The biggest source of revenue is __Borrowing and Other Liabilities__, which contributes 24% to government finances.
 
• Other major expenses include Interest Payments (20%) and Central Sector Schemes (16%).
 
• Other revenue sources include Income Tax (22%), GST & Other Taxes (18%), and Corporation Tax (17%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Borrowing and Other Liabilities**__

 __
 
• Borrowing accounts for a major portion of government revenue, allowing the government to fund its expenditures beyond tax collections.
 
• It includes loans from domestic and foreign markets, bonds, and other financial instruments.
 
 
 
• **States’ Share of Taxes and Duties**__
 __
 
• As per the Finance Commission recommendations, a portion of central taxes is devolved to states to ensure fiscal federalism.
 
• This helps states finance their developmental and welfare projects.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Components of Revenue and Expenditure**__
 
 
• **Income Tax (22%)** - A major revenue source collected from individuals and corporations.
 
• **GST & Other Taxes (18%)** - Includes Goods & Services Tax and indirect taxes.
 
• **Corporation Tax (17%)** - Levied on corporate profits.
 
• **Interest Payments (20%)** - Represents payments made by the government on its past borrowings.
 
• **Defence (8%)** - Allocation for national security, defence personnel salaries, and infrastructure.

questions.question: Which initiative has the Reserve Bank of India launched to address climate change risks and sustainable finance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**On Tap Cohort.**__

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is launching a dedicated 'On Tap' cohort on climate change risks and sustainable finance.**
 
• **This initiative will be part of RBI’s Regulatory Sandbox to encourage financial innovations in green finance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The 'On Tap' cohort aims to support capacity building, ecosystem development, and financing for sustainable projects.
 
• RBI is also planning to conduct a special ‘Greenathon’ focused on climate change and related aspects.

• Priority sector lending in India already supports credit flow to renewable energy and sustainable projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Regulatory Sandbox__

 __
 
• An initiative by RBI to allow fintech startups and financial institutions to test innovative financial solutions under regulatory supervision.
 
• Encourages development in digital payments, lending, and sustainable finance.
 
 
 
• Green Finance Challenges__
 __
 
• Higher credit risk due to new technologies with limited performance history.
 
• Need for technical know-how among financial institutions for risk assessment in green projects.
 
 
 
• Climate Change Risks in Finance__
 __
 
• Impacts financial risks including credit risk, market risk, and operational risk.
 
• Requires coordination among regulators, financial institutions, and government agencies.
 
 
 
• RBI's Role in Sustainable Finance__
 
 
• Facilitates policy and regulatory support for green finance initiatives.

• India's economy has shown consistent growth due to its focus on sectors like **technology, manufacturing, and renewable energy.**

• This growth rate helps India maintain its status as one of the fastest-growing major economies globally.

 __

• It was founded in **1944** and is headquartered in **Washington, D.C., USA.**

• The World Bank conducts in-depth research and publishes reports like the **India Development Update** to provide economic analysis and policy recommendations.

• It is influenced by factors like **domestic consumption, exports, government policies, and global economic trends.**

questions.question: What is the name of the new payment mechanism introduced by IRDAI for insurance premium payments via UPI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bima-ASBA.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **IRDAI has launched Bima-ASBA, a new payment mechanism for insurance premium payments via UPI.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bima-ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) allows policyholders to block funds in their bank accounts for premium payments.**
 
• The transfer of funds occurs only after the insurance policy is issued, ensuring smoother transactions.
 
• The new mechanism will be effective from March 1, 2025, as per the IRDAI circular.
 
• If a policy is not approved within 14 days, the blocked amount is automatically unblocked.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• How Bima-ASBA Works__

 __
 
• Customers authorize insurers to block a specific amount in their bank account before policy approval.
 
• The amount remains in the account but is blocked from being used until the insurer makes a decision.
 
• Upon approval, the amount is debited and transferred to the insurer.
 
• If the policy is rejected or canceled, the blocked amount is refunded to the customer.
 
 
 
• Benefits of Bima-ASBA__
 __
 
• Ensures secure premium payments without immediate deductions.
 
• Prevents unauthorized transactions and reduces payment failures.
 
• Allows policyholders to earn interest on the blocked amount while awaiting approval.
 
 
 
• IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)__
 
 
• The regulatory body overseeing India's insurance sector.
 
• Aims to protect policyholders' interests and promote the growth of the insurance industry.
 
• Introduces reforms like Bima-ASBA to enhance policyholder convenience.

questions.question: Under which condition did the RBI cancel the licence of Imperial Urban Co-operative Bank in April 2025?

options.text: Lack of liquidity and capital adequacy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lack of liquidity and capital adequacy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The RBI cancelled the licence of Imperial Urban Co-operative Bank due to inadequate liquidity and capital adequacy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Imperial Urban Co-operative Bank was unable to meet the financial requirements and its continuance was deemed prejudicial to its depositors.**
 
• 97.79% of the depositors are entitled to receive the full amount of their deposits up to Rs 5 lakh from the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC).
 
• The RBI also requested the Registrar of Cooperative Societies to wind up the bank and appoint a liquidator.
 
• The bank has been prohibited from conducting any banking operations, including accepting and repaying deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• A government agency that provides deposit insurance up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor for all scheduled banks and co-operative banks.

 __
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is responsible for regulating and supervising the functioning of banks to ensure financial stability and protect depositors' interests.
 
 
 
• Co-operative Banks__
 __
 
• Co-operative banks are financial institutions owned and managed by their members, serving the needs of communities and specific groups.
 
 
 
• Bank Liquidation__
 
 
• Bank liquidation is the process of winding up a bank’s operations, typically conducted by a liquidator, after a failure to meet financial requirements.

• The current account deficit for 2024-25 and 2025-26 is expected to remain within sustainable levels.

 __

• The committee uses tools like rate cuts to adjust growth trajectories in response to global and domestic factors.
 
 
 
• Global Economic Outlook__
 
 
• Refers to the projected performance of the global economy based on factors like trade policies, economic conditions, and international relations.

questions.question: What is the correct number of the budgetary estimate of the capital expenditure and capital receipt as per the Annual Financial Statement 2025-2026?

options.text: Capital Expenditure: ₹12.5 Lakh Crore, Capital Receipts: ₹17.1 Lakh Crore
Capital Expenditure: ₹13.5 Lakh Crore, Capital Receipts: ₹16.3 Lakh Crore
Capital Expenditure: ₹15.0 Lakh Crore, Capital Receipts: ₹16.9 Lakh Crore
Capital Expenditure: ₹11.2 Lakh Crore, Capital Receipts: ₹16.4 Lakh Crore

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital Expenditure: ₹11.2 Lakh Crore, Capital Receipts: ₹16.4 Lakh Crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Annual Financial Statement 2025-26 presents a budgetary estimate (BE) of ₹11.2 Lakh Crore for Capital Expenditure and ₹16.4 Lakh Crore for Capital Receipts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capital Expenditure for 2025-26 (BE) is estimated at ₹11.2 Lakh Crore, primarily for infrastructure, defense, and public sector projects.**
 
• **Capital Receipts for 2025-26 (BE) stand at ₹16.4 Lakh Crore, which includes borrowings and disinvestment proceeds.**
 
• For 2024-25, the Revised Estimate (RE) for Capital Expenditure was ₹13.5 Lakh Crore, while Capital Receipts stood at ₹16.3 Lakh Crore.
 
• Capital Expenditure includes funds for asset creation, such as roads, railways, defense procurement, and major development projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Capital Expenditure**__

 __
 
• It includes spending on **roads, highways, railways, defense equipment, and other infrastructure development.**
 
• It is aimed at asset creation and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Capital Receipts**__
 __
 
• Capital receipts include **borrowings, recovery of loans, and disinvestment proceeds.**
 
• They contribute to increasing liabilities or reducing assets.
 
 
 
• **Revenue vs. Capital Expenditure**__
 __
 
• **Revenue Expenditure:** Includes recurring expenses like salaries, pensions, and subsidies, which do not create assets.
 
• **Capital Expenditure:** Includes spending on infrastructure and asset-building projects.
 
 
 
• **Budget Deficit and Borrowings**__
 
 
• A major portion of capital receipts comes from borrowings, which contribute to the fiscal deficit.
 
• Managing the fiscal deficit is crucial for macroeconomic stability and growth.
